materials.text:
Now that you are holding onto a Node you have a few responsibilities:

First, you must read from the Node.Ready() channel and process the updates
it contains. These steps may be performed in parallel, except as noted in step
2.

1. Write HardState, Entries, and Snapshot to persistent storage if they are
not empty. Note that when writing an Entry with Index i, any
previously-persisted entries with Index >= i must be discarded.

2. Send all Messages to the nodes named in the To field. It is important that
no messages be sent until the latest HardState has been persisted to disk,
and all Entries written by any previous Ready batch (Messages may be sent while
entries from the same batch are being persisted). To reduce the I/O latency, an
optimization can be applied to make leader write to disk in parallel with its
followers (as explained at section 10.2.1 in Raft thesis). If any Message has type
MsgSnap, call Node.ReportSnapshot() after it has been sent (these messages may be
large).

Note: Marshalling messages is not thread-safe; it is important that you
make sure that no new entries are persisted while marshalling.
The easiest way to achieve this is to serialize the messages directly inside
your main raft loop.

3. Apply Snapshot (if any) and CommittedEntries to the state machine.
If any committed Entry has Type EntryConfChange, call Node.ApplyConfChange()
to apply it to the node. The configuration change may be cancelled at this point
by setting the NodeID field to zero before calling ApplyConfChange
(but ApplyConfChange must be called one way or the other, and the decision to cancel
must be based solely on the state machine and not external information such as
the observed health of the node).

4. Call Node.Advance() to signal readiness for the next batch of updates.
This may be done at any time after step 1, although all updates must be processed
in the order they were returned by Ready.

Second, all persisted log entries must be made available via an
implementation of the Storage interface. The provided MemoryStorage
type can be used for this (if you repopulate its state upon a
restart), or you can supply your own disk-backed implementation.

Third, when you receive a message from another node, pass it to Node.Step:

	func recvRaftRPC(ctx context.Context, m raftpb.Message) {
		n.Step(ctx, m)
	}

Finally, you need to call Node.Tick() at regular intervals (probably
via a time.Ticker). Raft has two important timeouts: heartbeat and the
election timeout. However, internally to the raft package time is
represented by an abstract "tick".

after.realization_summary: Leader proposal replication and current-term quorum commit; follower log matching.

after.purpose: Context validity and acquisition, transfer or loss of authority
after.realization_summary: Term and role transitions reset local support but preserve history.
Applied configuration replaces voter quorum and participant eligibility; construction not yet traced.

after.purpose: History, persistence and reconstruction of support
after.realization_summary: Ready and storage responses mediate durable history and support publication.

after.trigger: Caller applies ConfChange or snapshot restores ConfState
writes: Replace active configuration/progress and update learner status.
external_effects: Leader may recompute commit and broadcast; otherwise probes peers.
Removed or demoted leader steps down when stepDownOnRemoval is enabled.

cross_activity_effects.A1: Reinterprets acknowledgement quorum under the new voter sets and may advance commit.
cross_activity_effects.A2: Changes promotability and may remove current leader authority.

unknowns: Changer construction and caller sequencing still need tracing.
Can configuration application legally make the first current-term commit while a read is pending, and which path then releases it?

after.protocol_context: Local term, role, leader and vote
after.trigger: Campaign, election result, higher-term traffic or leadership loss
writes: reset clears votes, peer progress, transfer state and readOnly tracker, while retaining the log and commit index.
Campaign increments term and records self vote; becoming leader resets progress and appends a current-term empty entry.
important_branches: Pre-candidate transition does not increment term or reset the full state.
Higher-term pre-votes and granted pre-vote responses have special handling.
Old storage append responses cannot stabilize entries but may complete a committed snapshot.

after.protocol_context: Current leader term and active progress tracker
implementation_guards: Reject proposals during transfer or when local progress is absent; serialize configuration proposals against pendingConfIndex and joint state.
Ignore messages from senders without progress; Step filters obsolete terms.
writes: Append entries with current term and contiguous indexes.
Update peer Match and invoke maybeCommit against the active voter quorum and current-term log entry.
external_effects: Broadcast appends after proposal or commit advancement.
Only the successful MsgAppResp commit-advancement branch invokes releasePendingReadIndexMessages.
async_boundaries: Local self acknowledgement is queued until append completion; remote acknowledgements depend on the sender durability contract.

after.protocol_context: Ready batches, synchronous or asynchronous persistence
after.trigger: Ready accepted and completed by caller or storage response
writes: acceptReady records previous HardState and marks unstable/applying work in progress.
external_effects: Synchronous Ready exposes durable-dependent remote replies; self replies are held for Advance.
Asynchronous Ready emits append/apply work carrying completion responses.
async_boundaries: Caller must persist entries before sending synchronous Ready.Messages according to the Ready contract.
Async local messages must be reliable and ordered per storage target, with durable append completion before responses.

cross_activity_effects.A1: Controls when append and vote support can be published.
cross_activity_effects.A2: Persists term/vote and filters stale completion through Step.

unknowns: Package usage text permits current-batch send/persist overlap while Ready requires persistence first; applicability needs resolution.

formation.explanation: A leader assigns entry term/index, replicates and counts Match acknowledgements through active voter quorums. Current-term matching gates commit advancement. Followers match the preceding entry and reject committed-prefix conflicts; Ready exposes committed work to the caller.

context.explanation: Campaign and term handling acquire or lose leader authority. Real candidacy increments term; reset discards peer support and readOnly tracking. A new leader retains history, appends an empty current-term entry and conservatively delays configuration proposals until prior history is applied.

connection.explanation: Progress support is leader-context local, while committed history survives reset. Configuration application changes quorum interpretation and can itself advance commit. Persistence-qualified replies connect durable history to election and append support; old-term storage completion cannot discard potentially overwritten unstable entries.

open_details: Configuration-driven commit versus pending read release.
core_gaps: Trace actual voter-set construction and restoration, and caller ordering for application and completion.
Finish representative election aggregation, snapshot recovery, Node dispatch, and old/pending read handling before declaring overview usable.
